note: Curated X post summaries (live API unavailable or unpaid). Follow accounts below for newest posts.

items.title: The Hindu
items.summary: According to @the_hindu, the death toll and missing numbers are still climbing, with water levels in the Bhotekoshi rising again Sunday morning and tunnel rescues ongoing.

items.title: The Kathmandu Post
items.summary: More than a thousand family members have reached Pokhara to look through photos of the 102 bodies recovered after the Bhotekoshi flood. @kathmandupost notes a help desk on site offering free support with reports and transport.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: If you're checking on someone hurt in the Rasuwa Bhotekoshi or Trishuli flood, @NDRRMA_Nepal has posted updates on people still getting care in Kathmandu hospitals and those already discharged.

items.title: Embassy of India Beijing
items.summary: After the recent floods and mudslides in Tibet, authorities there have set up two 24-hour English hotlines for families looking for information on missing foreign nationals. The numbers are 0086-891-6817165 and 0086-183-0802-6705, per @EOIBeijing.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal shared the latest update on search, rescue and relief work for the Bhotekoshi flood, with details as of 9am on 14 Bhadra 2083.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal shared the details of the men rescued today.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal shared a list of foreign citizens rescued today, August 29. Check their account for the details.

items.title: MoFA Nepal
items.summary: @MoFANepal says 626 bodies have been recovered from the Bhote Koshi flood, with about 2400 people still unaccounted for. More than 4450 people have been rescued so far, including over 187 foreign nationals, and search teams are still working.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal has shared a list of Kathmandu hospitals treating people injured in the disaster and brought there for care, along with @moha_nepal.

items.title: MoFA Nepal
items.summary: Families checking on loved ones after the Bhote Koshi floods on 26 August can contact @MoFANepal, which reports 538 bodies recovered so far and ongoing searches for 511 people still missing out of 632 from 33 countries.

items.title: The Kathmandu Post
items.summary: Families searching for relatives from Rasuwa or Nuwakot may want to check morgues and temporary centers in Chitwan and Pokhara, where bodies have been arriving from upstream. @kathmandupost notes relatives are already looking there.

items.title: The Kathmandu Post
items.summary: In Nuwakot, some flooded villages are still waiting on relief while searches continue for homes and relatives buried after the Bhotekoshi surge. @kathmandupost has the local details.

items.title: MoFA Nepal
items.summary: If your family was affected by the Bhote Koshi flash flood in Rasuwa, @MoFANepal has set up an Emergency Control Room you can reach on WhatsApp or hotline at +977-9744441227 or +977-9744441228 from 7am to 10pm, or by email at emergency@mofa.gov.np.

items.title: NDTV
items.summary: @ndtv has a ground report from Rasuwa showing debris and washed-out spots along the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli, with Sikta Deo and Ranveer Singh. For casualty numbers, check with NDRRMA.

items.title: The Rising Nepal
items.summary: @therising_np reporters are on the ground between Dhunge Bazaar, Trishuli and Devighat. They say people had only minutes to leave after the alert went out around 8:55 this morning, and they’re following the rescue work with security teams.

items.title: MEA India
items.summary: Families with loved ones in Nepal can contact @MEAIndia’s control room at +91-11-23088718 or +91-11-23088719, WhatsApp +91-9968291988, or situationroom@mea.gov.in.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal is sharing rescue and coordination updates for the Bhotekoshi and Rasuwa flash flood on their official portals and the SETU platform. Families can check those for the latest information.

items.title: Nepal Police HQ
items.summary: @NepalPoliceHQ says their Unified Database has the official lists of people found, missing, or unidentified after the floods.

items.title: Embassy of India Kathmandu
items.summary: @IndiainNepal says the Indian embassy in Kathmandu is working with Nepalese authorities on search and rescue for Indian nationals caught in the flash floods around Rasuwa and Bhotekoshi. Families can contact the MEA control room or the embassy for help.

items.title: Parshuram Kaphle
items.summary: A journalist @journoprk is sharing thoughts on the Rasuwa and Bhote Koshi flash flood, wondering why early warnings from across the northern border didn't reach people in time.
